newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Pepsi sees slow but steady Venezuela return.
newsitem.headline: Pepsi sees slow but steady Venezuela return.

text.p: U.S. soft drinks giant PepsiCo will regain its footing in the Venezuelan market slowly but steadily, Pepsi chief executive Roger Enrico said Monday.
Pepsi was effectively ousted from the Venezuelan market in August by the surprise defection of its local bottler to Coca-Cola.
"It's going to take us a good two years to get back to where we were," Enrico told reporters. "But let me tell you, this will not be a one hundred yard dash ... we're here for a long time".

Pepsi -- which signed a 30/70 joint venture deal with leading Venezuelan foods and beverage company Polar in November to bottle and distribute cola -- expects sales to recover to 50 million cases by mid-1997 in a market estimated at 200 million cases.

Sales efforts will initially be limited to central Venezuela, which accounts for around 45 percent of the total market. Current production capacity stands at 35 million cases, which will rise to above 50 million as a new bottling plant at Caucagua is expanded.
"We're realistic, there are many barriers to our re-entry... it will be a gradual process," Enrico said.

Pepsi formerly dominated the Venezuelan soft drinks market. But after the suprise switch of the country's leading bottler, Grupo Cisneros Embotelladoras de Venezuela, to Coca-Cola in August, Pepsi products virtually disappeared from the Venezuelan market, where it once had an 80 percent share.
Although Venezuela contributed only 0.6 percent of company profits, the switch stung Pepsi.
"That's what happens in love and war, and sometimes in business," said Enrico.

Pepsi has said it will invest some $400 million over three years through the soft drinks subsidiary Sopresa of its new partner Polar, expanding production and distribution from a current 250 routes to 1,500 over the next.
"Of course, we were desperate to get back," Enrico said. "But we also view this as a great investment, we've always been greatly impressed by Polar."
